subject: Audit & Access Log retention and export — Q&A (logs export options)
messages:
From: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@acme-corp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2025-07-10T16:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on audit & access log retention + export capabilities

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Our security team asked for a short Q&A about your audit and access logs before we move further:

1) What are the default retention windows for (a) audit logs (admin actions, role changes, policy changes) and (b) access logs (request-level headers, IP, token usage)?
2) Can logs be exported automatically to our S3 or SIEM (Splunk/Datadog)? Are exports incremental/delta or full dumps?
3) Is retention configurable per-tenant or only globally? Can we set a 7-year retention for certain records?
4) On data deletion requests (e.g., user erase), how do logs referencing identifiers get handled — redaction vs deletion?

If you can send a short written summary we can attach to our vendor risk assessment. Appreciate it.

Best,
Rajiv
Senior InfoSec Manager
Acme Corp

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit & access log retention + export capabilities

Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A we typically provide; I’ve attached our retention whitepaper and an export API sample (see attachments). If you want, Marcus from infra can add implementation detail on the export pipelines.

Summary (short):
- Defaults: audit logs = 365 days, access/request logs = 90 days.
- Export: Yes — push to S3, Snowflake, or via long-lived webhook/forwarding to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). Exports can be scheduled (daily full) or streamed (near-real-time).
- Config: Retention is configurable at the customer org level for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted accounts can request extended retention for an additional commitment.
- Deletion: We support redaction or deletion on request. For audit integrity we keep an immutable record internally for compliance windows but can redact PII/identifiers on exported copies; for Private deployments customers control deletion.

Attachments: redwood-audit-log-retention.pdf (policy + retention table), export-api-sample.json (example payload).

Next step: If you want SIEM integration specifics, Marcus can reply with endpoints and auth patterns.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@acme-corp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-12T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit & access log retention + export capabilities

Rajiv — quick technical notes to supplement Lauren’s summary:  

1) Endpoints & formats: We offer a managed export service that can ship logs in JSONL or Parquet to customer S3 buckets (server-side encryption supported). For SIEMs we provide a syslog/FluentD forwarding endpoint and a Splunk HEC sample.

2) Export modes:  
  - Scheduled full export (nightly): full set for the day in Parquet/JSONL.
  - Incremental delta: uses last-seen cursor; downstream receives only new events.
  - Streaming: near-real-time via secure HTTPS with backpressure and retry semantics.

3) Retention controls:  
  - Hosted: default audit=365d, access=90d. Admins can request extensions (90d, 1y, 3y) under an enterprise SLA.  
  - Dedicated/Private: per-tenant retention policy managed via config UI or API up to customer-determined limits (we have customers running 7+ years).

4) Deletion & redaction:  
  - Deletion requests for user data: we remove PII from logs and replace with opaque reference tokens in hosted setups; for legal/regulatory holds we can quarantine records under an enterprise agreement.
  - Immutable audit trail: for enterprise compliance we can maintain a signed audit digest (hash chain) while redacting identifiers — this preserves sequence/integrity while removing sensitive fields.

Auth & security: Exports use short-lived signed URLs for S3; SIEM forwarders use mTLS or HMAC tokens depending on customer preference. All exports are logged and observable in the Console.

If you want a quick runbook for how to wire an S3 sink + CloudTrail correlation, I can drop a sample Terraform and a minimal FluentD config.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@acme-corp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Compliance Team <compliance@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2025-07-13T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit & access log retention + export capabilities

Thanks Lauren/Marcus — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups from Compliance:  

- For our vendor risk assessment we need a statement we can attach saying: “Default retention windows and options to extend to 7 years under enterprise contract; exports via S3/HTTP/Syslog with encryption in transit and at rest.” Can you provide a short canned paragraph we can include?
- For deletion: we need clarity that when PII is redacted from logs you still retain enough context to perform security investigations (i.e., timestamp, action, actor role) — can you confirm which fields you will redact vs retain by default?

If you can send those two items we’ll move to legal procurement.

-Rajiv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@acme-corp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit & access log retention + export capabilities

Rajiv — looping in short, approved language and field-level guidance from our compliance team:  

1) Canned paragraph (suitable for vendor assessment):
"Redwood Inference default retention for audit logs is 365 days and for request/access logs is 90 days. Customers on enterprise contracts or Dedicated/Private deployments may configure extended retention periods (options include 1 year, 3 years, and custom terms up to 7+ years) subject to contractual agreement. Log export capabilities include scheduled daily exports and streaming delivery to customer-managed S3 buckets (JSONL/Parquet), Snowflake ingestion, and SIEM integration (Syslog/FluentD/Splunk HEC). All exports support TLS in transit and AES-256 server-side encryption at rest."
2) Field-level redaction default behavior (hosted accounts):
  - Redacted by default: user email, user_id (PII), IP addresses when requested for privacy, session tokens, and any request payloads marked as PII.
  - Retained by default: timestamp, action type (e.g., "model.generate", "policy.change"), actor role (admin/user/service), resource identifier (opaque id), request outcome/status, and correlation_id for tracing.  

We can provide a sample export schema showing the exact JSON fields; Marcus can attach that or we can share a short CSV mapping if helpful. Let us know the fastest way to get this into your vendor packet — we can also sign an NDA if Compliance prefers.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
